subject: English
passage: Ancient Athens, a city-state in which citizens personally gathered in assemblies to vote on legislation during the fifth century BCE, is considered a direct democracy—a political system in which the people themselves exercise governing authority rather than delegating it. Political scientists classify direct democracies as distinct from representative democracies, or systems in which citizens elect officials to govern on their behalf. ______ modern Switzerland (1800s-present) combines frequent citizen referendums with an elected federal assembly.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words, governments are classified according to who exercises authority:
choices.B: For example, representative democracies have long dominated modern governance:
choices.C: Of course, the distinction is not always so neat:
choices.D: Likewise, representative democracies are elected-official systems:

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. "Of course, the distinction is not always so neat" logically signals that the information in this sentence—that modern Switzerland combines frequent citizen referendums with an elected federal assembly—is true despite the previous presentation of a clear binary classification between direct democracies and representative democracies.
